policy.forbidden: the profile path of the account that runs the probe, and its leaf directory: zero hits, always - the probe computes it, this file never stores it

flutter.reason: the plugin calls the Flutter engine's C API by name; those symbols are in its import table and are not ours to rename.

dart.reason: a third-party JNI bridge built from the Flutter engine's sources; the strings are its type and API names.

flutter.reason: the AOT snapshot names the engine entry points and embedder API it links against. Raised 50 -> 54 on 2026-11-12: what the substring matches here is the framework's own platform-channel names - flutter/textinput, flutter/lifecycle, flutter/keydata, flutter/mousecursor, flutter/restoration, flutter/keyboard, plugins.flutter.io/path_provider, dev.leanflutter.plugins/screen_retriever - and the four that appeared since 2026-11-03 are channels the app's newer window and tray UI opens. None of the 54 carries a path.

dart.reason: the snapshot keeps the Dart VM's own type and library names; obfuscation renames ours, not the VM's.

pubspec.reason: the package name from pubspec.yaml is baked into the snapshot: it names the product, not the machine. Raised 1 -> 2 on 2026-11-12: both occurrences are error messages in the snapshot that end in the file name - "...is expected until you remove this plugin from pubspec.yaml" and "...is not in the asset list (see pubspec.yaml \"assets:\")" - and the second one is this project's own asset gate talking, not a path to the machine that built it.

flutter.reason: the prebuilt Flutter engine is a third-party binary we do not compile; its strings are the framework's own and name no account.

dart.reason: the Dart VM inside that engine names itself; removing it would mean rebuilding Flutter from source.

cargo.reason: rustc records the source directory of every crate it compiles; the account prefix is remapped to /build by the 2026-11-02 fingerprint sweep, so what is left is the toolchain's own layout (.cargo\registry\src\...), which says which crates built the file, not who built it. Raised 1242 -> 1243 on 2026-11-03 (the LOW-row slice), and the cause was measured instead of assumed: counting the crate-path strings in engine\target\release\mics-engine.exe against the shipped engine gives 1240 against 1239, and the one path that appeared is windows-strings-0.5.1\src\bstr.rs - the DPAPI store in secrets.rs routes the API keys through windows-dpapi, whose error path monomorphizes one more windows-strings module. That is a dependency's own source layout, not the account that built the file: the forbidden-path check stayed green in the same run. Raised 1243 -> 1244 on 2026-11-12: the distinct cargo-bearing strings differ from the 2026-11-09 build by exactly one, and it is the remapped form of a path that build still carried with the profile prefix in it - today the string reads `/build\.cargo\registry\src\index.crates.io-1949cf8c6b5b557f\serde_json-1.0.154\src\error.rs` - so the extra occurrence is a repeat inside the toolchain's own layout rather than a new kind of string, and the same run kept the forbidden-path check green (zero hits).

dart.reason: the package manifest names dartjni.dll among the files it lists, so the substring appears once: that is a shipped file name, not the Dart VM living in this binary.

flutter.reason: the manifest names every shipped file and 54 of them sit under data\flutter_assets\, with flutter_windows.dll making 55: these are the paths the start-up self-check hashes, not the toolchain that built the engine.

rustc.reason: the engine's panic, version and RUST_BACKTRACE strings name the compiler that produced them; none of them carries a path.

flutter.reason: the C++ runner calls the Flutter C API by name (DartProject, the view controller, the messenger).
